New BMW M3 Gearing Up To Rival AMG's C 63 and Audi's RS 5 – Rendering
6 photos
Photo: Kolesa
It’s been one month since BMW pulled the wraps off the new-generation 3 Series . Well, it’s not entirely new, because it features familiar underpinnings, as it is based on an updated version of the old car’s platform.
We are talking about the CLAR, and it’s not the Linie Grosse, which is the foundation stone of the old 7 Series, the demised 8 Series, the previous X5, outgoing X6, current X7, and XM, but the Linie Klein. In its previous configuration, it was used by the old 3 Series, as well as the previous-gen 5 Series, 6 Series, old X3, X4, Z4, Toyota GR Supra, and other models. And this construction will also be used on the upcoming M3.
BMW’s premium compact sports sedan will obviously live on to see a new generation, albeit a Neue Klasse one inside and out. But of course you already know that, because we have encountered plenty of prototypes in the open, and some of these have been used as blank canvases by the pixel altering crowd to create realistic digital illustrations. Thus, not only do we know that the new BMW M3 is indeed in the making, but we also know what it will look like, for the most part, anyway.
After all, it is not tricky at all to imagine the new-gen BMW 3 Series with a more aggressive design and a few other modifications, with some styling cues inspired by the M Concept Neue Klasse that was unveiled at the beginning of the year. Thus, if you feel like these renderings, which were signed by Kolesa’s Nikita Chuyko and released online a few days ago, are somewhat familiar, that’s because they use the new 3er as a starting point, as well as some features virtually borrowed from the study mentioned above.
Photo: Kolesa The car in question features a new hood that has a vented design, as well as an entirely new bumper at the front with extra lights on the sides, and it is these that have been inspired by the BMW M Concept Neue Klasse. The central part of the bumper, namely the air intakes, are quite similar to those of the regular 3er, and so is the grille, for that matter, as well as the headlights, including the yellow DRLs, which are a thing on the current range-topping version of the new-gen BMW 3 Series family, the M350 xDrive.
At the rear, we can see that this imagined new-gen BMW M3 sports a bumper that was also inspired by the one of the show car. It also has a pair of fake vents in the middle, a diffuser less aggressive than that of the M350, and a much chunkier ducktail spoiler. The taillights, and trunk lid are the same, and, quite surprisingly, so are the quad exhaust tips, from what we can tell. The wheels, however, are new, and very M-like, for that matter, and the car features an orange paint finish, a black roof, and other black details on the outside.
The quoted outlet is not famously known for releasing CGIs of the cockpits of its rendered models, but it is not hard to imagine what the interior of the all-new BMW M3 will look like. That’s because it will have the same dashboard panel as other Neue Klasse models, including the regular 3 Series, the i3, iX3, facelifted 7 Series, and new X5. This also means the Panoramic iDrive display stretching from one pillar to the other on the base of the windshield, as well as the same infotainment system.
Photo: Kolesa Sure, the screens will likely feature dedicated load screens and submenus, but overall, they will be the same. The steering wheel, on the other hand, should be different and a lot sportier, and we also expect the car to feature bucket seats for the driver and front passenger, as well as dedicated upholstery and trim, some M colors here and there, and a few other bits and bobs that will further separate the cabin of the new M3 from the regular 3 Series.
A familiar straight-six engine will sit under the hood of the upcoming BMW M3 , with twin turbocharging, a 3.0-liter displacement, and likely mild-hybrid assistance. We do not yet know any details about its power and torque, but let’s not forget that this model’s biggest rivals in the class, the Audi RS 5 and the Mercedes-AMG C 63, offer north of 600 horsepower, so it is only natural to expect the Munich company’s sports sedan (and station wagon) to have a similar output.
Word on the street is that the all-new BMW M3 will debut in 2028, roughly one year after its battery-electric sibling , the mechanically unrelated M3 Electric (based on the Neue Klasse platform), and we wouldn’t be surprised if it ends up looking like this CGI-infused model. But do you dig the design ?
